parts.name: body loop

physics.Basic_description: The main D-shaped spine of the carabiner, appearing as a white-anodized aluminum tube with a smooth matte finish.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the primary structural strength and load-bearing loop for clipping onto anchors or gear.
physics.Grasped_description: A parallel jaw gripper can securely grasp the straight spine section of the loop from the side.
physics.reason: High-strength climbing carabiners are typically hot-forged or extruded with significant material thickness but are not solid blocks; modeled as a thick-walled shell to approximate mass correctly.

parts.description: The main D-shaped spine of the carabiner, appearing as a white-anodized aluminum tube with a smooth matte finish.
parts.function: Provides the primary structural strength and load-bearing loop for clipping onto anchors or gear.

parts.name: nose lug

physics.Basic_description: A small protrusion at the top of the body loop, matching the white anodized aluminum finish.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the catch point where the gate latch engages to close the carabiner.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and integral to the body to be grasped independently; gripper would contact the main body instead.
physics.reason: Small forged feature integral to the main body loop, effectively solid material at this scale.

parts.description: A small protrusion at the top of the body loop, matching the white anodized aluminum finish.
parts.function: Acts as the catch point where the gate latch engages to close the carabiner.

parts.name: gate bar

physics.Basic_description: The straight swinging bar that closes the opening, finished in white anodized aluminum.
physics.Functional_description: Swings open to allow clipping and closes to secure the connection.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped by a gripper to manually open the gate, though typically the body is grasped first.
physics.reason: Gate bars are typically solid extruded or machined rods to withstand lateral loading.

parts.description: The straight swinging bar that closes the opening, finished in white anodized aluminum.
parts.function: Swings open to allow clipping and closes to secure the connection.

parts.name: gate latch

physics.Basic_description: The tip of the gate mechanism, appearing as a small white metallic component.
physics.Functional_description: Interfaces with the nose lug to lock the gate in the closed position.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a viable grasp target due to small size and location at the gate tip.

parts.description: The tip of the gate mechanism, appearing as a small white metallic component.
parts.function: Interfaces with the nose lug to lock the gate in the closed position.

parts.name: hinge pin

physics.Basic_description: A tiny pin at the base of the gate, likely steel, appearing as a small grey/white dot.
physics.Functional_description: Serves as the pivot axis for the gate's rotation.
physics.Grasped_description: Impossible to grasp independently; internal/fastening component.
physics.reason: Pins are inherently solid cylindrical components.

parts.description: A tiny pin at the base of the gate, likely steel, appearing as a small grey/white dot.
parts.function: Serves as the pivot axis for the gate's rotation.

parts.name: lock sleeve barrel

physics.Basic_description: Cylindrical sleeves with knurled texture (rendered as ridges) on the gate, appearing light grey/white.
physics.Functional_description: Rotates or slides to lock the gate mechanism, preventing accidental opening.
physics.Grasped_description: The knurled surface provides excellent friction for a gripper to rotate or slide the sleeve.
physics.reason: Locking sleeves are tubular components that fit over the gate bar, necessarily hollow to allow rotation/sliding.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
